clue.text: Not favouring an animal oriental folk chain

parts.note: con is the case against, as in pros and cons
a cat is a common animal
E is short for eastern
a nation is a people or folk

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to a chain of animal-loving eastern peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A concatenation is a linked series of things joined one after another, much like links of a chain.

clue.text: In debt yet again and tense as a result

parts.note: to do something over is to do it again
a drawn face looks strained and tense

explanation.surface: Someone back in the red once more and anxious because of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links debt and tension as cause and effect, but the two words simply join side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn bank account has had more money taken out than it held, leaving its owner owing the bank.

clue.text: Holds one's own ceremonial robes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: manages or deals successfully with difficulty
second meaning: long cloaks worn by priests at services

explanation.surface: Someone stands firm while dressed in their formal vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who copes manages under pressure, and copes are also the long capes worn by clergy in processions.

clue.text: Three altogether attempt to impound it in error

indicators.note: to impound something is to shut it up inside an enclosure

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: letters in error are in the wrong places and need setting straight

parts.note: these two words are the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trio attempts to lock something away, mistakenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it in' looks like part of the phrase 'impound it', but those two words are the fodder and 'error' signals their shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinity in Christian doctrine is three persons in one God, three that are united as one whole.

clue.text: An uplifting fragrance now in production

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upward
a fragrance is a scent

explanation.surface: A cheering perfume has just gone into manufacture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into existence, beginning to be made or developed.

clue.text: Send a car?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to enrapture or carry away with emotion, or to convey
second meaning: a car is an example of a vehicle for getting about

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a car is only one example of the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport is to convey or to delight, and a car is one form of transport or vehicle.

clue.text: A poem about Greek theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A piece of verse written about a Greek playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like the link to the subject of the poem, but it supplies the second chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was an ancient Greek roofed building for musical performances, later lending its name to cinemas.

clue.text: Still synchronised

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nevertheless, all the same

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'nevertheless' when conceding a point and 'simultaneously' when events coincide.

clue.text: Publicity drive meant set being replaced

indicators.note: being replaced suggests putting things back in new positions

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign intended to replace a stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: An advertisement is a notice promoting a product, so it is a piece of publicity.

clue.text: Dismantled ship and stole booty

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart and could be rebuilt differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the joining word

explanation.surface: Pirates broke up a vessel and made off with the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' sits inside the fodder phrase but only joins the two words; it is not part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoils are goods taken by a victor, plunder seized in war or theft.

clue.text: Better have the last word with the dunderhead!

parts.note: amen ends a prayer, so it is literally the closing word

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the start of the word dunder, before its head marker

explanation.surface: Win the argument by having the final say over a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a whole word, but it splits so that 'head' points at the first letter of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to improve or correct it, so the verb better works as a swap.

clue.text: The underworld guy's seen around these days

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps itself on both sides of another

parts.note: a guy is a he, and the 's gives he's
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A man is spotted hanging around hell nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek realm of the dead, the classical name for the world below.

clue.text: Popular European city church getting down to the basics

parts.note: what is in is fashionable
Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A well-liked church in a European city returns to fundamentals.
explanation.definitionFit: In essence means basically, considering only the fundamental nature of a thing.

clue.text: A place fit only for pigs occupied by exceptionally lean man

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has it living inside

parts.words: A place fit only for pigs
parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, also any filthy place

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at an unusual form of the following word

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A filthy hovel is taken over by a very skinny fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley is a man's first name, and crosswords often use 'man' for any male forename.

clue.text: A source of amusement to those in love

parts.words: A source of amusement to those in love

parts.note: setter's reading: the proverb says love laughs at the tradesman who fits bolts and keys

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'love laughs at locksmiths' means no lock can keep lovers apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying that love laughs at locksmiths makes this tradesman the butt of lovers' amusement.

clue.text: Had in mind a trifle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: considered or believed, past tense of think
second meaning: a little, as in 'a ___ too sweet'

explanation.surface: Someone was thinking about a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' tempts towards the British pudding, but here 'a trifle' means slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of think, and 'a thought' is an idiom for a small amount.

clue.text: The spirit shown by everyone involved in bridge

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside something else

parts.note: a gantry is a bridge-like frame carrying signals or a crane
all means everyone

explanation.surface: All the card players display courage at the bridge table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is a structure spanning a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is courage or chivalrous bravery, the brave spirit someone displays.

clue.text: There's no extension for this little beast!

definitions.text: There's no extension for this little beast!

parts.words: There's no extension for this little beast!
parts.note: surface reading: a small creature that is refused a phone line or a deadline

parts.words: There's no extension for this little beast!
parts.note: setter's reading: the extension missing is a tail, on a breed from an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is in the Irish Sea; its native cat breed is born tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's native feline is famous for having no tail, the extension at its rear.

clue.text: Examines a note presented in an Italian port

parts.note: to try a case is to examine it in court
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone tests a memo handed over in an Italian harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a seaport city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Comes to an agreement over the seating

definitions.meaning: second meaning: long wooden benches with high backs

explanation.surface: People reach a deal about where everyone will sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old wooden bench with arms and a high back.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to reach a deal, and settles are high-backed benches, a form of seats.

clue.text: Get excited having a drink with the players inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to sup is to sip, and a sup is a mouthful of drink
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Getting worked up over a drink in the company of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: To steam up is an idiom for becoming agitated or worked up, like a boiling kettle.

clue.text: A roundabout means of gaining admission

definitions.text: A roundabout means of gaining admission

parts.words: A roundabout means of gaining admission
parts.note: surface reading: an indirect way to get in somewhere

parts.words: A roundabout means of gaining admission
parts.note: setter's reading: a gate that literally revolves as you pass through it

explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like 'devious', but it is meant literally: the gate rotates.
explanation.definitionFit: This revolving barrier at stadiums and stations admits people one at a time as its arms turn.

clue.text: Revolting individual given a step up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who rises up in revolt
second meaning: the vertical part of a stair

explanation.surface: A disgusting person is handed a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' tempts as 'disgusting', but it means rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is one who rises in rebellion, and also the upright board between stair treads.

clue.text: Insist 150 go by train

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
to train a gun on a target is to aim it

explanation.surface: Someone insists on 150 people travelling by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway, but it is the verb for pointing a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim is to assert or maintain firmly that something is so.

parts.note: to care is to show concern
V, versus, means against or opposing

explanation.surface: Showing concern but not hostile, someone makes a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, as in slicing meat or shaping wood with a blade.

clue.text: Well-qualified persons, really tip-top people

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree
A1 means first-rate, its digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Highly educated people really are the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, an ethnic group or nation.

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium
taken as written
to mar is to spoil or wreck
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans are a British helpline charity; the Good Samaritan of the parable cared for a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan is a helper of people in need, after the parable, so someone who cares for others.

clue.text: An old bird's cheaper to X-ray, surprisingly!

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters arrive in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet finds an elderly bird is unexpectedly inexpensive to scan.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeopteryx is a Jurassic fossil creature, one of the earliest known birds, so very old indeed.
